- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a drop, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3) and forecast is falling, adjust downward by 3–5% to avoid premature mean reversion.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a “mean reversion bias” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If forecast is significantly below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, increase forecast by 2–4% per day to avoid underestimating rebound.
